title: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster (STS-51-L)
summary: On 28 January 1986 the Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds into its STS-51-L ascent, killing all seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. A failed rubber seal in a solid rocket booster joint began the sequence. The shuttle fleet was grounded for more than two years and the presidential commission found that most causes lay in human errors of judging data, communicating and deciding.

uncertainty.note: Single day; breakup occurred 73 seconds after liftoff.

where.modern_name: Launch Complex 39B (Pad B), Kennedy Space Center, Florida, USA (pin marks the launch pad; the vehicle broke apart over the Atlantic off the Florida coast)
where.historical_name: Launch Pad B (39B), NASA Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States

importance.justification: Loss of a crewed orbiter and seven lives; grounded the shuttle fleet for over two years and reshaped NASA's safety practice.

audience_note: Loss of life: the seven crew members of Challenger were killed in the accident.

beats.caption: Challenger lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on the morning of 28 January 1986 on mission STS-51-L.
Seventy-three seconds into the flight the vehicle broke apart; all seven crew members died.
The fleet lost one of its orbiters and was grounded for more than two years, with greater attention to safety afterwards.
